title: The Agile Manifesto: the four values
blurb: Recall the four values of the Agile Manifesto, pair each left-hand item with its right-hand item, and explain what 'over' means.
question: A board member says, 'The Agile Manifesto means we can stop writing documents and drop the plan.' Using the four values, what is wrong with this statement?

teach.h: A short statement with a long reach
teach.body: The Manifesto for Agile Software Development was written in 2001 by a group of software practitioners. Its four values sit at the heart of agile, and the PRINCE2 Agile book presents them in its chapter on agile (2.2, Table 2.1). Each value compares two things: the item on the left is valued more, but the item on the right still has value.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.2, Table 2.1; agilemanifesto.org (2001)

head: Valued more (left)
Still valued (right)
teach.caption: Learn them as fixed pairs: the exam swaps halves to make wrong options.

teach.body: The Manifesto ends by saying that while there is value in the items on the right, the items on the left are valued more. So agile teams still use processes and tools, write documentation, agree contracts and make plans. What changes is the priority when the two pull against each other.

rows.label: Plans
values: Plan, then adapt as you learn

teach.body: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools: a quick conversation usually solves more than another form or ticket, and tools should serve the team. Working software over comprehensive documentation: something users can try tells you more than a long specification. On a non-software project, read 'working software' as working products, such as a usable service or a finished room design.

Customer collaboration over contract negotiation: customer and supplier work together on what is needed rather than arguing over clauses. Responding to change over following a plan: when users or the market tell you something new, adapting beats sticking rigidly to the original plan. PRINCE2 Agile still plans, at release and iteration level, and expects plans to change.

children.edge: work it out or argue clauses?
children.label: Customer collaboration

teach.body: At Tidewater Insurance, project manager Olumide Bakare is running a claims-app project. Developers sort out a confusing rule by talking to a claims handler instead of logging a ticket. The team demos a working claim form rather than circulating a 60-page design. The supplier and Tidewater reshape scope together. When users ask for photo upload, the next release changes to include it.

teach.text: Watch for swapped halves, such as 'customer collaboration over following a plan' or 'working software over contract negotiation'. And never accept 'the right-hand items have no value': the Manifesto says they still have value, just less than the left.

items: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.
Responding to change over following a plan. The right-hand items still have value; the left are valued more.

summary: You can now recall the four values of the Agile Manifesto as exact pairs and explain that the right-hand items still matter but are valued less. You can also recognize which value a project decision reflects.

A.q: Which of these is one of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
options: Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Customer collaboration over following a plan
A.why: The first value is individuals and interactions over processes and tools.

whyNot.0: This reverses the value: individuals and interactions are valued more.
whyNot.2: This mixes two values: customer collaboration is valued over contract negotiation.
whyNot.3: This reverses the value: working software is valued over comprehensive documentation.

A.q: Identify the missing words in the following value of the Agile Manifesto. Customer collaboration over [?].
A.why: The value is customer collaboration over contract negotiation.

whyNot.1: Comprehensive documentation is paired with working software.
whyNot.2: Following a plan is paired with responding to change.
whyNot.3: Processes and tools are paired with individuals and interactions.

A.q: How does the Agile Manifesto treat the items on the right-hand side of each value?
options: They should be removed from agile projects
They are valued equally with the left
They still have value, but the left is valued more
They apply to waterfall projects, not agile ones
A.why: The Manifesto says there is value in the items on the right, but the items on the left are valued more.

whyNot.0: The right-hand items still have value; agile teams keep using them.
whyNot.1: The left-hand items are valued more, so the two are not equal.
whyNot.3: The values do not split items between waterfall and agile projects.

B.q: In the Agile Manifesto, responding to change is valued over what?
B.why: The fourth value is responding to change over following a plan.

whyNot.0: Contract negotiation is paired with customer collaboration.
whyNot.1: Comprehensive documentation is paired with working software.
whyNot.2: Processes and tools are paired with individuals and interactions.

B.q: A supplier and its client meet weekly to reshape the scope together, rather than renegotiating the contract clause by clause. Which value does this reflect?
options: Responding to change over following a plan
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
B.why: Working together on what is needed, instead of arguing over clauses, is customer collaboration over contract negotiation.

whyNot.0: Scope may change, but the behaviour described is collaboration instead of contract negotiation.
whyNot.2: Nothing here concerns demonstrating products instead of documents.
whyNot.3: The point is the customer-supplier relationship, not people versus tools within a team.

B.q: Two developers resolve a confusing requirement by talking directly to a user, instead of logging a query in the tracking tool. Which value does this reflect?
options: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Responding to change over following a plan
B.why: Choosing a direct conversation over a tool-based process is individuals and interactions over processes and tools.

whyNot.1: No contract is involved; the choice is between talking and using a tool.
whyNot.2: The plan is not being changed; the choice is about how people communicate.
whyNot.3: The choice is not between a working product and a document.

C.q:
Which two statements about the Agile Manifesto are correct?
1. It sets out four values.
2. It says plans have no value in agile work.
3. It values working software over comprehensive documentation.
4. It values contract negotiation over customer collaboration.
C.why: There are four values (1), and working software is valued over comprehensive documentation (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: plans still have value; responding to change is valued more.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: plans keep their value, and customer collaboration is valued over contract negotiation.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 reverses the value: customer collaboration is valued more.

C.q: A board member says, 'Agile means we stop producing documents.' Which response reflects the Agile Manifesto?
options: Documents are valued more than working products
Documents matter most where contracts apply
Documents still have value; working products more
C.why: Working software is valued over comprehensive documentation, but the Manifesto says the right-hand items still have value.

whyNot.0: The Manifesto does not replace documentation; it values it less than working products.
whyNot.2: The Manifesto does not tie the value of documents to contracts.

C.q: After a review, a team changes its release plan to add a feature users have just requested. Which value does this reflect, and which item is valued less?
options: Responding to change; processes and tools
Responding to change; following a plan
C.why: Adapting the plan to new user needs is responding to change, which is valued over following a plan.

whyNot.0: Following a plan is paired with responding to change, not customer collaboration.
whyNot.1: Responding to change is right, but its pair is following a plan, not processes and tools.
whyNot.3: Working software is paired with comprehensive documentation.

reteach.title: Four see-saws
reteach.question: How do you remember which items pair together, and which way each value leans?

blocks.body: Picture four see-saws. On each, the left seat is heavier but the right seat is not empty. People and conversation outweigh process and tools. A working product outweighs a thick document. Working with the customer outweighs haggling over the contract. Adapting to change outweighs sticking to the plan. Learn each see-saw as one unit so you never swap the seats between them.

letters.word: Individuals and interactions (vs processes and tools)
Responding to change (vs following a plan)

blocks.text: The right-hand items are valued less, not discarded. Any option saying plans, documents, contracts or tools have no value is wrong.

explain.h: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
explain.body: People talking and working together solve problems faster than routing everything through a process or tool. Processes and tools still help; people come first.

test.q: In the Agile Manifesto, what are individuals and interactions valued over?
test.why: The first value is individuals and interactions over processes and tools.

whyNot.1: Following a plan is paired with responding to change.
whyNot.2: Contract negotiation is paired with customer collaboration.
whyNot.3: Comprehensive documentation is paired with working software.

explain.body: Something users can try is the best evidence of progress and the best source of feedback. Documentation still has a place, but not at the expense of working products.

test.q: A team demonstrates a working prototype to users instead of circulating a long design document. Which value does this reflect?
options: Responding to change over following a plan
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
test.why: Showing a working product rather than a long document reflects working software over comprehensive documentation.

whyNot.1: The plan is not being changed here.
whyNot.3: The choice is between a product and a document, not people and tools.

explain.body: Customer and supplier work as partners on what is needed. Contracts still exist and matter, but working together beats arguing over terms.

test.q: Customer collaboration is valued over what?
test.why: The third value is customer collaboration over contract negotiation.

whyNot.0: Following a plan is paired with responding to change.
whyNot.1: Processes and tools are paired with individuals and interactions.
whyNot.2: Comprehensive documentation is paired with working software.

explain.h: Responding to change over following a plan
explain.body: When users or circumstances reveal something new, adapting is valued over sticking rigidly to the original plan. Plans still matter; they are expected to change.

test.q: Which value of the Agile Manifesto pairs with 'following a plan'?
test.why: Responding to change is valued over following a plan.

whyNot.1: Customer collaboration is paired with contract negotiation.
whyNot.2: Working software is paired with comprehensive documentation.
whyNot.3: Individuals and interactions are paired with processes and tools.
